text:
ana: Heads-up — there is a container in the kitchen labeled "Jerry's lunch" but someone left a ladle of chili in it. Smells amazing but slightly ominous :eyes:
liam: oh no. I left a note that said "not mine" but also ate 2 forks worth so ??? :sweat_smile:
maya: lol fork thief. who put a name on communal chili anyway.
jordan: may have been me. i microwaved it, put the lid back on, then labeled it because i panicked about office etiquette. apologies if it was actually Jerry's. :grimacing:
sam: can confirm there is now a sticky note that reads "Jerry? if this is yours, reclaim before 3pm or it goes to personnel (aka hungry people)" :joy:
nana: (ops-bot) fridge-temp: 4°C — no spoilage detected.
liam: also proposing an emergency snack policy: 
```
- write contents, date, and intended eater on container
- if ambiguous, add "communal" and set a 24h claim timer
- offenders donate a bag of chips
```
maya: i second. also demand cilantro be banned from office chili (personal vendetta) :stuck_out_tongue:
jordan: vote poll: who thinks we should adopt the snack policy? react with :thumbsup: or :thumbsdown:
nana: (ops-bot) poll created: "Adopt snack policy?" — :thumbsup: 3, :thumbsdown: 1
liam: winner winner chili dinner.
sam: will label my future culinary experiments "communal" and maybe include a warning if it contains cilantro.
maya: thanks for the heads-up, whoever brought it — culinary risk-taker of the week: :trophy: :laughing: 
jordan: note to self: next time write "DO NOT TOUCH — TESTING FERMENTATION" and see who reads the label. :kidding:
liam: can we at least get a tiny whiteboard by the fridge? quick notes > sticky napkins.
nana: (ops-bot) whiteboard request logged — facilities ticket #F-4721
ana: (ops-bot) reminder in 2h: check for reclaimed food.
